question: How should model architecture, open vs closed choice, context/KV-cache strategy and light fine-tuning be matched to agent roles in a multi-agent system?
contributions: Maps encoder-only, decoder-only, MoE and reasoning models to agent roles

results.claim: Closed-model prices reach $150 input / $600 output per million tokens (o1-pro); open models about $0.3 / $3 via low-cost cloud providers.
results.setup: Prices per million tokens, undated, no provider named; open figure for models over 200B parameters
results.quote: Closed models can cost up to $150 for input and $600 (o1-pro) for output per million tokens, while open models fall around $0.3 for input and about $3 for output per million tokens when used via low-cost cloud providers even for models over 200B parameters.

limits: Early Release draft, raw and unedited; no experiments, benchmarks or ablations.
Prices and model choices are undated and will age.
Code is partial (tools, graph wiring and routing omitted).
Thinking budget given as 1024 in the Qwen snippet and 1536 in the team setup.
rope_scaling example loads ModernBERT in vLLM and claims 32k to 128k; ModernBERT natural length is 8192 per Table 4-4, so the example is inconsistent.
practices: Staff agents by role: fast decoder-only for workers, a reasoning model for the analyst, encoder for scoring, a deliberate LLM as supervisor (Putting It All Together).
Enable thinking for planning, decomposition, tool selection, verification; disable for short low-risk turns (Thinking modes).
Set a thinking budget of 1000+ tokens for non-trivial reasoning; raise for math, code, multi-tool plans (Thinking budget).
Monitor KV cache hit ratio and memory pressure; use paging or trimming (KV caching).
Any structural context change must trigger selective cache invalidation; preallocate static system prompts to keep partial cache persistence (KV caching).
Use a sliding window or prefix trimming near max context; also mitigates the haystack problem.
Start with managed APIs, then move to self-hosted open models as the team and needs mature (Open vs. Closed).
Combine quantized weights, LoRA/adapters and PEFT for open-model pipelines (Optimizing Open Source Models).
